Generate and benchmark synthetic data in a Shiny app

Source: R/app.R
run_synthcheck_app.Rd

run_synthcheck_app() opens an app that walks through the whole workflow without code. It opens on an About tab that explains the purpose of the app, lists what it can do and produce, shows an animated picture of a language model answering survey items and starts a guided tour (the tour needs the cicerone package). The tour follows the path chosen in the first step.

Usage

run_synthcheck_app(
  real = NULL,
  synthetic = NULL,
  host = "127.0.0.1",
  port = NULL,
  launch.browser = TRUE
)

synthcheck_app(real = NULL, synthetic = NULL, hosted = sc_is_hosted())

Arguments

real

optional data frame of real responses, loaded into the Compare tab. With real data given, the first step starts on "Yes, I have real data".

synthetic

optional data frame of synthetic respondents (for example from generate_synthetic() or read_synthetic()), loaded into the Compare and Pretest tabs.

host, port

where to serve the app. The default serves it on your own computer only.

launch.browser

open the app in a browser?

hosted

run in hosted mode (see above)? The default is TRUE when the option synthcheck.hosted is TRUE, the environment variable SYNTHCHECK_HOSTED is "true", or the app runs on shinyapps.io or Posit Connect.

Value

Invisibly, when the app is closed with its Close button: A list with synthetic (the generated data), benchmark (the authenticity_benchmark() result, if one was run), pretest (the synthetic_pretest() result, if one was run), interviews (the cognitive_interview() result, if one was run), path ("real", "pretest" or NULL), instrument and personas. synthcheck_app() returns a Shiny app object.

Details

First step: The About tab asks one question: Do you already have real responses to this instrument? The answer chooses one of two paths, and it can be changed at any time, so you can come back with real data later and benchmark the same synthetic data.

  • Yes, I have real data: The fourth tab is Compare, the benchmark against real people.

  • No, not yet: The fourth tab is Pretest, followed by Interviews, so Export becomes the sixth tab. Compare is hidden.

The tabs, in order (with real data: 1 to 4 and 5. Export; without: 1 to 3, 4. Pretest, 5. Interviews and 6. Export):

  • 1. Instrument: Upload an item table or use a built-in instrument (the IPIP-HEXACO, or one of three short scales with well-documented item problems: The Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, the DASS-21 and the Mini-IPIP; see sc_builtin_instrument()), and set the response scale and instructions (sc_instrument()).

  • 2. Personas: Type, upload or build the personas that take the instrument (sc_personas(), sc_persona_grid()). Both upload panels offer a template to fill in. The templates are also in the package: system.file("templates", "instrument_template.csv", package = "synthcheck") and "personas_template.csv".

  • 3. Models: Add Anthropic, OpenAI or local Ollama models with their temperature (or several temperatures, one model each), enter API keys, choose the number of attempts and respondents, and run generate_synthetic() with a progress bar and the time left. Before a run with paid models, the app shows its estimated cost (estimate_cost()) and asks you to confirm. Answers are kept in the response cache (sc_cache()), so the same run again is repeatable and free; choose to reuse, refresh or skip saved answers, or clear them.

  • 4. Compare (with real data): Load real data and run authenticity_benchmark(), with gg_benchmark(), gg_behaviour() and a plain-language summary per model (summarise_benchmark()).

  • 4. Pretest (without real data): Run synthetic_pretest() on the generated data, with gg_pretest() and a plain-language summary (summarise_pretest()). Compare the flags across models, temperatures or personas to see whether they hold. It is pilot screening, not validation.

  • 5. Interviews (without real data): Run cognitive_interview() with the personas and models of tabs 2 and 3, on the items the pretest flagged or on items you choose (the pretest is optional), and read the summary (summarise_interviews()), the plot (gg_interview()) and the transcripts. A screening aid, not a substitute for cognitive interviews with real people.

  • Export: Download a results report (HTML or PDF, see write_report()), the synthetic data (CSV, JSON, RDS or Excel), the benchmark or the pretest and interviews, and an R script that repeats the analysis.

API keys typed into the app stay in memory for that session only: They are never written to the saved data, the run settings or the R script. Keys set as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY (for example in .Renviron) are used without being shown. New to API keys? The article Getting an API key walks through signing up with OpenAI or Anthropic, adding credit, keeping the key private and setting a spending limit, and the Models tab links to it next to the key fields.

Runs go to a background R process when callr is installed, so the app stays responsive and the Stop button works. Every attempt is written to the output folder as soon as it is done.

Hosting the app: run_synthcheck_app() always runs the full app on your own computer. synthcheck_app() returns the same app as an object for a server such as Posit Connect Cloud or shinyapps.io. On a server it runs in hosted mode: Ollama is not offered (local models need the package on your own computer), keys from the server's environment are never used, each visitor types their own keys, which stay in that browser session's memory, and the generated files go to a temporary folder that is deleted when the session ends. The article Hosting the app walks through a deployment.

The benchmark compares models and supports decisions about them. It does not show that synthetic data can replace a field test.

See also

generate_synthetic(), authenticity_benchmark()

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  res <- run_synthcheck_app()
  res$benchmark
}
# the app object for a server, as in an app.R file
app <- synthcheck_app(hosted = TRUE)
